description.summary: Send contestants onto the stage — but any you sweep up join your troupe as penalty points. Fewest points wins!

content.title: Overview
content.text: Pageant is a game for 2-6 players. The deck has 66 contestants in 6 sash colors, each numbered 0-10. You start with 5 cards in hand, and 6 contestants open the show in a lineup on stage. On your turn you add one contestant to the END of the lineup — but that may send others walking off into YOUR troupe. Collected contestants are penalty points, so you want as FEW as possible.

content.title: Taking a turn
content.text:
Play one card to the end of the lineup, then draw back up to 5.

The card's number N sets how far its 'gaze' reaches: the last N contestants already on stage are safe. Among every contestant BEFORE those, you must collect any that either share your card's color OR have a number equal to or less than N.

Play a 0 and the whole stage is fair game; play a 10 and almost everyone is safe.

content.title: Ending the pageant
content.text:
The end is triggered the moment a player has collected at least one contestant of all 6 colors, OR the draw pile runs out.

Once triggered, every other player takes one last turn (no drawing). Then each player discards 2 cards from their hand and adds the rest to their troupe. Now you score.

content.title: Fewest points wins
content.text:
Add up the numbers on every contestant in your troupe — that's your score, and the LOWEST score wins (a tie is broken by who collected fewer cards).

The saving grace: for each color, whoever collected the MOST of that color flips those cards face down, and they count just 1 point each instead of their face value. So dominating a color is good; a scattered handful of high numbers is what sinks you.

content.title: Majorities & 2-player rule
content.text: Ties for a color majority all flip. In a 2-player game you need at least 2 MORE of a color than your opponent to claim its majority — otherwise nobody flips and both of you pay full value.

content.title: Your troupe at a glance
content.text:
A summary card at your seat always shows how many of each color you have collected, so you can see who is running away with a color.

If you run out of time on your turn, a random legal card is played for you.
